import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Create a figure and an axes object
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# Create a bar plot to visualize the survival rate by Passenger Class and Sex
# The 'survived' column contains 0s and 1s, so the mean represents the survival rate.
sns.barplot(data=df, x='pclass', y='survived', hue='sex', palette='viridis', ci=95)

# Add descriptive labels and title
plt.xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Survival Rate', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Titanic Survival Rate by Passenger Class and Sex', fontsize=14)

# Customize x-axis tick labels for better readability
plt.xticks(ticks=[0, 1, 2], labels=['First (1st)', 'Second (2nd)', 'Third (3rd)'])

# Add a legend for 'sex'
plt.legend(title='Sex', loc='upper right')

# Set y-axis limit for survival rate (0 to 1)
plt.ylim(0, 1)

# Add a grid for better readability
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
